questions.explanation: The Moon’s differential gravitational pull contributes strongly to Earth’s tides; the Sun also contributes.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the Earth's rotation and its revolution is correct?
options: It takes the Earth longer to rotate on its axis than revolve around the sun.
It takes the Earth longer revolve around the sun than to rotate on its axis.
It takes the Earth longer to rotate around the sun than revolve on its axis.
It takes the Earth longer revolve around its axis than to rotate around the sun.
questions.explanation: Earth rotates once in about a day and revolves around the Sun in about a year.

options: the moon travels around Earth in an orbit shaped like an oval
Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the moon
the Moon blocks sunlight from reaching the sun
you only see part of the Moon
questions.explanation: Earth lies between Sun and Moon and blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon.

questions.prompt: The Earth's axis is tilted at an angle of 23.5°. Imagine if it WASN’T tilted, and was perfectly straight. Which of the following statements would be TRUE?
options: Earth would have the same seasons as it does now
The length of a year would change
Earth would not have any seasons at all
The length of the day would change
questions.explanation: C is the intended school answer: removing axial tilt removes the familiar tilt-driven seasons. Small effects from orbital eccentricity could remain.

questions.prompt: The length of time it takes the moon to revolve around the Earth once is called a
questions.explanation: A month; the sidereal orbital period is about 27.3 days, while the phase cycle is about 29.5 days.

questions.prompt: As you move further away from Earth, its gravitational force field:
questions.explanation: Earth’s gravitational field becomes weaker with increasing distance from its centre.

questions.prompt: The moon casts a shadow on Earth during a ___________?
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon’s shadow falls on Earth.

questions.prompt: When the North Pole is tilted TOWARD the Sun, it is?
questions.explanation: The Northern Hemisphere has summer when tilted toward the Sun.
